illustrae.name: The intrinsic apoptotic pathway is initiated by cellular stress, which activates BH3-only proteins (Bid, Bim, Noxa, PUMA) that trigger Bax/Bak translocation to the outer mitochondrial membrane. Bax/Bak oligomerization forms a pore, releasing cytochrome c into the cytoplasm, where it binds Apaf-1 and ATP to assemble the apoptosome. The apoptosome activates caspase-9, which cleaves and activates executioner caspases-3 and -7 to execute apoptosis

Panel 1 (top left): vector delivers a functional gene to a Blue (#0072B2) nucleus, with a Bluish Green (#009E73) activation arrow to a cell cycle arrest symbol. Panel 2 (top right): vector delivers an enzyme gene; an Orange (#E69F00) prodrug molecule enters the cell and is converted to a Vermillion (#D55E00) toxic metabolite with a cell death symbol. Panel 3 (bottom left): vector delivers a Sky Blue (#56B4E9) siRNA strand that binds a mRNA molecule with a Vermillion (#D55E00) inhibitory flat-head arrow blocking oncogene output. Panel 4 (bottom right): vector delivers a cytokine gene; a cytokine molecule exits the cell and activates a T-cell shape via Bluish Green (#009E73) arrow. Light gray panel borders separate the four strategies. Flat vector, white background, Okabe-Ito palette, unannotated, no text labels.

Connect all three panels with left-to-right process arrows. Label: 'Acetylation,' 'EZH2,' 'HDAC,' 'DNMT,' 'CTCF,' 'Nucleosome,' 'TSG.' Flat vector style. White background. Clean sans-serif font. illustrae.name:
A clean, educational single-panel diagram showing the intrinsic apoptotic pathway taking place inside a cross-section of a cell for an undergraduate cancer biology textbook.
Draw a large oval representing the cell boundary. Inside, show the following spatial layout from top to bottom:
Top area — Nucleus:
Draw a nucleus with a cracked or damaged DNA strand inside, labeled 'DNA Damage / Cellular Stress.' Show a small arrow pointing outward from the nucleus to small protein labels: 'p53 → PUMA / Noxa' and 'Bim / Bid activated.' These are shown as small floating protein shapes near the nucleus.
Middle area — Mitochondrion:
Draw a large mitochondrion in the center of the cell with clearly visible inner and outer membranes. Show BH3-only proteins (Bid, Bim, PUMA) arriving at the mitochondrial surface with a small arrow labeled 'BH3 proteins activate Bax/Bak.' On the outer membrane, show a pore formed by 'Bax/Bak' labeled clearly. From this pore, show multiple small yellow circles labeled 'Cytochrome c' spilling into the cytoplasm with a curved release arrow.
Bottom area — Cytoplasm:
Show the released cytochrome c molecules clustering with a large ring-shaped complex labeled 'Apoptosome (Cytochrome c + Apaf-1 + ATP).' From the apoptosome, show an arrow to 'Caspase-9 activated,' and from caspase-9 show two arrows branching to 'Caspase-3' and 'Caspase-7.' End with a bold red starburst or box labeled 'APOPTOSIS.'
Number each event sequentially (1 through 5) with small circled numbers to guide the student's eye through the pathway. Add a simple legend at the bottom identifying cytochrome c, Bax/Bak pore, apoptosome, and caspases.

illustrae.name:
A clean, educational single-panel diagram showing the extrinsic apoptotic pathway taking place inside and at the surface of a cross-section of a cell for an undergraduate cancer biology textbook.
Draw a large oval representing the cell boundary. Organize the diagram from top to bottom:
Top area — Cell Surface:
Draw the cell membrane as a thick horizontal band at the top of the cell. On the outside of the membrane, show a small labeled ligand molecule 'FasL / TNF' binding to a receptor protein embedded in the membrane, labeled 'Death Receptor (FAS / TNFR).' Use a lock-and-key style docking to make the binding visually clear. Add a circled number '1' and label: 'Death ligand binds death receptor.'
Upper middle area — DISC Formation:
Just below the membrane on the cytoplasmic side, show the death receptor's intracellular tail recruiting adapter proteins labeled 'FADD.' Below FADD, show multiple 'Procaspase-8' molecules clustering around the complex. Draw a bracket around the entire assembly and label it 'DISC (Death-Inducing Signaling Complex).' Show a cleavage symbol (scissors icon or dotted line) on procaspase-8, producing 'Active Caspase-8.' Add a circled number '2.'
Middle area — Two Downstream Branches:
From active caspase-8, draw two branching arrows:

Left branch (direct pathway): Arrow pointing straight down to 'Caspase-3 / Caspase-7 activated,' labeled 'Direct route.' Add a circled number '3.'
Right branch (amplification loop): Arrow pointing to a small protein labeled 'Bid cleaved → tBid.' Show tBid migrating toward a small mitochondrion drawn on the right side of the cell. Show cytochrome c being released from the mitochondrion with a small label 'Connects to intrinsic pathway.' Draw this branch with a dotted line to indicate it is a secondary amplification route. Add a circled number '4.'

Bottom area — Outcome:
Both branches converge at the bottom into a bold red starburst or box labeled 'APOPTOSIS.' Add a circled number '5.'
Add a simple legend at the bottom identifying: death receptor, FADD, DISC, caspase-8, caspase-3/7, tBid, and the mitochondrial amplification loop.

The central rung-3 C carries a damage marker: a jagged black crack down the middle of the block and a bright-red warning outline/glow. A dashed circle surrounds damaged base, with a label "deaminated C — damaged base" at the damaged base. A single smooth purple enzyme is attached to the left strand of the double helix, one rung above the danaged base labeled "DNA glycosylase." with a dashed vertical arrow runs down the left side of the ladder, labeled "scanning." ensure landscape panel of 1920x1080 pixels.

illustrae.name: Three-panel educational diagram illustrating sentinel lymph node biopsy of the breast. All panels show a flat schematic cross-section of breast tissue with a visible tumor mass labeled 'Primary Tumor.' Panel 1 labeled 'Step 1 — Injection': show a syringe injecting material near the tumor site. Label injection site 'Radioactive substance and/or blue dye injected near tumor.' Show the injected material beginning to spread from the injection site as small dots or colored diffusion arrows. Panel 2 labeled 'Step 2 — Detection': show the same breast cross-section with a handheld gamma probe icon held over the breast surface — label 'Radioactivity detection probe.' Show a dotted trail from the injection site leading to two or three small oval lymph node icons — label the first node reached 'Sentinel lymph node — first node cancer cells likely to reach.' Show remaining nodes labeled 'Secondary lymph nodes.' Highlight the sentinel node with a distinct color (blue or green fill) to indicate it has taken up the dye/tracer. Panel 3 labeled 'Step 3 — Removal and Pathology': show the breast cross-section with the tumor removed (dashed outline where tumor was — label 'Tumor removed') and the sentinel lymph node removed (dashed outline — label 'Sentinel node removed'). Show the removed node beside the breast as a flat icon with a magnifying glass symbol — label 'Node examined for cancer cells.' Add a two-outcome branch: 'Cancer cells present → further lymph node dissection' and 'No cancer cells → no further node removal.' Connect all three panels with left-to-right numbered arrows. Label: 'Primary Tumor,' 'Injection site,' 'Sentinel lymph node,' 'Gamma probe,' 'Radioactive tracer / blue dye.' Flat vector style. White background. Clean sans-serif font. Scientific oncology textbook
